title: Understanding PCA
text: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is a technique used to emphasize variation and bring out strong patterns in a dataset. It projects data onto new axes (principal components) that maximize variance.

title: Interpreting the Scatter Plot
text: The scatter plot shows a negative correlation between 'mpg' and 'age'. This means as 'age' increases, 'mpg' decreases.

title: Analyzing the Point Plot (f.ii)
text: The point plot (f.ii) shows two points with a larger spread. This could indicate a projection onto a principal component with more variance.
